samples.text:
The maps shows a part of a city harbour in 1985 and after it was redeveloped in 2025. Overall, the area was industrial in 1985 but in 2025 it is used for living and leisure.

In 1985, there were two warehouse and a factory next to the harbour, and a customs office in the east. There was two cranes at the edge of the water. A goods railway went across the area from west to east and there was a storage yard in the north-west, near to Dock Road.

In 2025, the warehouses have been replaced by two blocks of apartments. The factory was converted into an art gallery and the customs office became a restaurant. Also, the storage yard is now a park and a car park, and the railway changed to a cycle path. Along the water there is a new waterfront promenade, and instead of cranes there is two marina jetties now. Dock Road and the harbour stayed the same.
samples.why: Clear but simple overview · all key changes included though presented as a list · mechanical linking (Also) · adequate vocabulary · errors in plurals, agreement and prepositions that do not obscure meaning.

samples.text:
The maps compare an area of a city harbour in 1985 with the same area after its redevelopment in 2025. Overall, the harbour has been transformed from an industrial zone into a residential and leisure area, with most former industrial buildings either replaced or converted to new uses.

In 1985, the area was dominated by industry. Two warehouses and a factory stood beside the harbour, with a customs office further east, and two cranes were positioned at the water's edge. A goods railway crossed the site from west to east, and to the north of it there was a large storage yard next to Dock Road.

By 2025, the two warehouses had been demolished and replaced by apartment blocks, while the factory had been converted into an art gallery. The customs office has also been turned into a restaurant. The storage yard has made way for a park and a car park, and the railway line has become a cycle path. Along the water, a waterfront promenade has been created and the cranes have been replaced with two marina jetties. Only Dock Road and the harbour itself remains unchanged.
samples.why: Clear overview · logical before-and-after structure with key features highlighted · good cohesion · appropriate vocabulary (dominated, converted) · mostly accurate, with a slight tense inconsistency and an agreement slip.

samples.text:
The maps illustrate the redevelopment of a city harbour area between 1985 and 2025. Broadly speaking, a working industrial waterfront has been reinvented as a residential and leisure district, with almost every industrial feature either replaced or adapted for a new purpose.

In 1985, the waterfront was lined with two warehouses in the west and centre and a factory in the east, beyond which stood a customs office. Two cranes stood at the water's edge, and a goods railway ran parallel to the harbour, separating these buildings from a storage yard that bordered Dock Road to the north.

By 2025, the warehouses had been replaced by two apartment blocks, and the factory had been converted into an art gallery, while the former customs office now houses a restaurant. The railway has been turned into a cycle path following almost the same route, and the storage yard to its north has been divided between a park and a car park. At the water's edge, a promenade now runs the full length of the harbour, and the two cranes have disappeared, with two marina jetties extending into the water slightly further east. Dock Road and the harbour itself are the only features left entirely unaltered.
samples.why: Sharp overview of the change in function · features compared precisely, including positions · cohesion natural and varied · sophisticated, accurate vocabulary (reinvented, adapted, houses) · wide range of structures, error-free.
